ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 3 — Focused Visit (Follow-up) — Jesse Owens

code.originalText: Day 1 of cycle 2 of nivolumab with carboplatin and pemetrexed: toxicity, immune-related adverse event monitoring, smoking abstinence and prehabilitation

text.paragraph: Day 1 of cycle 2 of nivolumab with carboplatin and pemetrexed. [S]

Mr. Owens comes before his second cycle, three weeks after the first. He has not smoked since the morning of cycle 1. Varenicline gave him mild nausea for the first week, which settled by taking it after food; his dreams are vivid but not upsetting. After cycle 1 he was tired for four days and mildly nauseated for two, needing ondansetron twice. He has had no diarrhea, rash, cough beyond his usual, breathlessness, headache, or yellowing. He has been to five pulmonary rehabilitation sessions and walks most mornings. The hepatitis and HIV tests before cycle 1 were negative. He has had no thoughts of self-harm. [S]

text.paragraph: Vital signs recorded on 2026-06-24; see the Vital Signs section. [S]

tr.td: Well; weight 75.8 kg; blood pressure 126/78, pulse 74; oxygen saturation 96 percent
Light touch and vibration normal in the feet

Solid, spiculated 2.9 cm nodule in the left upper lobe with an enlarged (1.6 cm) left hilar lymph node on today's low-dose screening CT, Lung-RADS 4X (very suspicious); no symptoms of lung cancer. PET-CT, tissue diagnosis and thoracic oncology review booked
S — Synthetic presenting screening finding in a long-term smoker. Superseded by the diagnosis at the second visit.

Adenocarcinoma of the left upper lobe of the lung, cT1c N1 M0, stage IIB (AJCC 8th edition), resectable: 2.9 cm primary with a positive left interlobar (11L) node on EBUS; mediastinal nodes 4R, 4L and 7 negative; no metastases on PET-CT or brain MRI. PD-L1 tumor proportion score 40 percent (22C3); KRAS G12C mutation; no EGFR, ALK, ROS1, BRAF, MET exon 14, RET, NTRK or HER2 alteration
S — Synthetic histology, stage and biomarkers linked to his documented adenocarcinoma of the left lung; in the modern episode it is found by screening while still resectable.
Nicotine dependence, cigarettes: a pack a day for 35 years (35 pack-years); smokes his first cigarette within 30 minutes of waking; two attempts to stop, each lasting a few weeks without medicine
S — Synthetic modern entry linked to his documented smoking; superseded at the visit after surgery by nicotine dependence in early remission.

Left upper lobe adenocarcinoma, stage IIB, on chemoimmunotherapy before surgery (C34.12). Cycle 1 tolerated well; counts adequate (neutrophils 4.1, platelets 214), kidney and liver tests normal, thyroid normal. No immune-related adverse event. [S]
Cycle 2 today with the same doses.
Thoracic surgery review next week.
Restaging CT after cycle 3.

Nicotine dependence, on varenicline (F17.210). Three weeks abstinent; nausea settled with food. [S]
Continue varenicline 1 mg twice daily.
Quitline calls continue.

TSH 2.6, free T4 1.1; ALT 28, AST 25, bilirubin 0.5; creatinine 1.0, eGFR 84; glucose 101 non-fasting the morning after dexamethasone
Baseline and before each immunotherapy infusion (CMID); for symptoms

Missed: the CMID schedule calls for cortisol before each infusion, but the cycle 2 order set did not include it and it was not drawn. No harm is expected: he has no fatigue beyond the days after chemotherapy, no low blood pressure, low sodium or dizziness. Corrective action: cortisol added to the standing order set for cycle 3 and to the blood tests before surgery

Outcome by 2026-05-26: PET-CT in three days, brain MRI in four, EBUS in eight, tumor board in ten; PD-L1 and tissue sequencing back by the consultation, 15 days after the scan [S]
Stop smoking completely before treatment starts and stay stopped. In progress; target 2026-09-30 [S]
Three cycles of chemoimmunotherapy before surgery without a delay of more than one week and without an immune-related adverse event of grade 2 or higher. In progress; target 2026-08-05 [S]

Back to walking 3 km most mornings by three months after surgery. In progress; target 2026-09-30 [S]

J Clin Oncol 2021;39(36):4073-4126 (PMID 34724392) (2021); Tobacco Smoking Cessation in Adults, Including Pregnant Persons: Interventions (2021)

Follow-up: Cycle 3 in three weeks. Thoracic surgery review next week. Visit with restaging CT after cycle 3. Call the oncology line for any warning sign. Next scheduled visit 2026-08-05: after three cycles: restaging CT, decision for lobectomy, thyroid result and surgical preparation. [S]
